articles.title: Jaypal Malviya Wins World Silver, Secures India's First LA 2028 Quota
articles.excerpt: The little-known pistol shooter scored 242.2 in the Doha final behind China's Hu Kai, and India's women took team silver the same morning.
articles.image_caption: Jaypal Malviya, left, holds his silver medal on the podium at the ISSF World Championships in Doha, with gold medalist Hu Kai of China, centre, and bronze medalist Jindrich Dubovy of Czechia. Malviya's second place secured India's first quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
articles.nri_angle: Malviya's quota opens India's Los Angeles 2028 account — the Games diaspora fans in the US will host in their own backyard.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rajasthan Royals, Lucknow Super Giants in Talks Over Multi-Player Trade
articles.excerpt: Cricbuzz reports a three- or four-player swap agreed in principle, with names under wraps: a pacer and possibly a spinner to Jaipur, a batter or all-rounder the other way.
articles.nri_angle: IPL trade season is followed closely by diaspora fans ahead of the December 16 mini-auction in Goa; this reported swap would reshape two squads before retentions close on November 17.

articles.title: Dravid and Sehwag's Sons Open India's U-19 Asia Cup Campaign Against Nepal
articles.excerpt: Anvay Dravid and Aaryavir Sehwag are in India's 15-man squad, led by Lakshya Raichandani, for the ACC Men's U-19 Asia Cup opener in Muscat on Friday.
articles.nri_angle: The tournament runs in Muscat, Oman, from November 5 to 14, with India's group also containing Pakistan and the UAE — fixtures diaspora fans can follow from the Gulf and beyond.

articles.title: Tickner Backs New Zealand to Bounce Back Against India in Wellington ODI
articles.excerpt: Bowled out for 185 in Auckland, New Zealand must level the series on Saturday without Devon Conway. Blair Tickner, their No. 11 top-scorer in the opener, says the side moves on fast.
articles.nri_angle: The second ODI starts at 7:30 a.m. IST on Saturday, November 7 in Wellington — an early-morning watch in India and a Saturday fixture for diaspora fans in New Zealand.

articles.title: Jangoo, Forde and Mangru Earn Maiden West Indies Central Contracts
articles.excerpt: Cricket West Indies handed retainers to 15 men and 15 women for 2026-27, with John Campbell back for the first time since 2019 and every deal tied to a qualification target.
articles.nri_angle: West Indies cricket holds a deep following among Indo-Caribbean and Indian diaspora fans, and Jangoo's record stand came against Sri Lanka with his latest hundred against Bangladesh.

articles.title: India Come From Behind to Beat Japan 4-1, Win Sixth Asian Champions Trophy
articles.excerpt: Trailing from the third minute in Mohali, India equalised through Shilanand Lakra in the 42nd minute and scored three times in the final quarter to complete a hat-trick of titles.
articles.image_caption: India and Japan contest the Men's Asian Champions Trophy final in Mohali. India came from a goal down to win 4-1 and claim a record sixth title.
articles.nri_angle: A record sixth Asian Champions Trophy title, won from behind at home in Punjab, gives Indian hockey fans abroad a championship run defined by late goals and an unbeaten tournament.

articles.title: Tanvi Patri, 15, First Indian Woman to Reach Youth Olympic Badminton Final
articles.excerpt: The Odisha shuttler beat Japan's second seed Yuzuno Watanabe 21-14, 11-21, 21-19 in 54 minutes, assuring India its first women's singles medal at the Youth Olympic Games. China's Yi Xin Zhang awaits in the final.
articles.image_caption: Tanvi Patri poses with a medal and certificate at a junior badminton championship. The 15-year-old from Odisha has become the first Indian woman to reach a Youth Olympic Games badminton final.
